message.content:
**Uno – Game Rules (Quick Overview)** | Section | What Happens | Key Points | |---------|--------------|------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points. | Points are earned by winning rounds; you can stop playing at any time and keep your current total. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Turn the top card of the draw pile face‑up to start the discard pile. | If the first card is an action card, its effect applies immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two,” the next player draws two cards). | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a “Reverse” card is played). | The direction changes each time a “Reverse” card is played. | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn, you may play one card from your hand that matches the color, number, or symbol of the top discard card. | You can also play a Wild card (any color) or a Wild Draw Four (any color + force next player to draw four). | | **If You Can’t Play** | Draw one card from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately. | If you still can’t play, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. | Wild Draw Four can only be played if you have no other playable card of the same color. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have one card left, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. | If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. | That player scores points based on the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to your total. | First to reach 500 points wins the game. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep an eye on colors** – If you’re holding many cards of a single color, try to play them early to avoid being stuck later. 2. **Use Wilds strategically** – Save Wild Draw Fours for when you’re sure you’re the last card left; they’re powerful but risky. 3. **Watch opponents** – If someone keeps drawing, they might be holding a Wild Draw Four; be ready to challenge if you suspect they’re bluffing. Enjoy your game!
